newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire kills holiday for Dr. King.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire kills holiday for Dr. King.

text.p: The New Hampshire Legislature Tuesday, for the 10th time since 1979, killed a measure the would have established an official holiday for slain civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King.

House lawmakers supporting a King holiday failed by one vote, 178-177, to approve a Senate-passed bill establishing a Martin Luther King Civil Rights Day holiday. The action means New Hampshire will retain its distinction of being the only state in the nation without an official holiday for the civil rights leader.
Coretta Scott King, King's widow,, called on the legislature last fall to finally pass a holiday in her husband's name.
But lawmakers Tuesday not only killed the possibility of a holiday for King this year, they passed a motion ensuring the issue cannot be considered until 1999.

New Hampshire has celebrated a Civil Rights Day holiday for the past four years. Supporters of the state holiday say King should not be singled out for special attention among those who fought for civil rights.
